figures.finding: The laws of New South Wales, the applied law jurisdiction, are in force in Norfolk Island, subject to suspension or amendment by a section 19A Ordinance and yielding to Acts and the Island's own enactments; the Island's Employment Act 1988 is one such enactment.

figures.finding: The Island's Employment Act sets no minimum age: an employer may not employ a person under fifteen during compulsory school hours or between 11 p.m. and 6 a.m., nor for more than 20 hours in a school week or 40 in another, apprentices over fourteen excepted; New South Wales, whose laws apply, likewise sets no general minimum age (Legal Aid NSW, in the AU file).

sources.said: An employer must not employ a person under the age of 15 years— (a) during any hours that the person is required by law to attend school; or (b) at any time between the hours of 11.00 pm on one day and 6.00 am on the next.

an employer must not employ a person under the age of 15 years— (a) for more than 20 hours during a week in which the person is required by law to attend school; or (b) for more than 40 hours during any other week.

figures.finding: New South Wales's rule, applied here unless an Ordinance suspends it (none was found, but the 2016 Ordinance wasn't read for it): a child performer or model is anyone under sixteen, whoever employs one in entertainment needs the Children's Guardian's Authority, and film and television work is capped by age (4 hours a day under 3 years, 6 at 3 to 7, 8 at 8 to 15, within 6 a.m. to 11 p.m., 12 hours between shifts); on top, the Island's Employment Act bars school hours and nights under fifteen; the rule names performers and models, not writers or directors.

figures.finding: In New South Wales, whose law applies, a person under eighteen may sign a contract that is for his benefit and that he understands; no share of a child's earnings is set aside; the rule is general contract law, reaching writing and directing as well.

value.binding: for the minor's benefit and understood (NSW Minors (Property and Contracts) Act 1970 ss 18-19)

figures.finding: Only an individual of at least eighteen may be appointed a director of a company registered under the Corporations Act (whether the Act's own area takes in Norfolk Island wasn't settled; a reading, as for Christmas Island).

sources.said: Only an individual who is at least 18 may be appointed as a director of a company.
